content.value_statement: Frontend teams can miss keyboard, semantic, and screen reader requirements. This skill guides AI agents to build accessible UI components.
actual_capabilities: Guides semantic HTML choices for landmarks, headings, buttons, links, articles, and sections.
Checks forms for associated labels, accessible names, and clear input relationships.
Reviews keyboard navigation, focus order, visible focus states, and modal focus management.
Prompts WCAG contrast checks for text, interface controls, and important visual states.
Supports ARIA usage for complex patterns where native HTML is not sufficient.
limitations: Does not run automated accessibility scanners by itself.
Does not replace manual testing with screen readers and keyboard-only navigation.
Does not guarantee legal compliance for every product or jurisdiction.
Relies on available project code and design context for accurate recommendations.

use_cases.title: Review React Components
use_cases.description: Find accessibility gaps in component markup, labels, focus states, and ARIA usage before release.

use_cases.title: Build Accessible Forms
use_cases.description: Create forms with clear labels, validation messaging, keyboard support, and screen reader friendly structure.

use_cases.title: Audit Interactive UI
use_cases.description: Evaluate dialogs, menus, buttons, and dynamic content for focus control and keyboard behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Check A Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single UI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for accessibility issues. Focus on semantic HTML, labels, keyboard support, contrast, and screen reader behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Improve A Form
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate improvement of form markup and validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this form for accessibility. Ensure every input has a label, validation is announced, and keyboard users can complete the flow.

prompt_templates.title: Fix A Modal Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of focus management in interactive UI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this modal or dialog flow. Check focus trapping, initial focus, escape behavior, return focus, announcements, and keyboard interaction.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Feature End To End
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced accessibility pass across a full user workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend workflow for WCAG accessibility risks. Provide prioritized fixes for semantics, focus, contrast, headings, ARIA, and assistive technology support.

output_examples.input: A React form with placeholder-only labels and inline validation messages.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing labels, unclear error announcements, weak focus states, and recommends explicit labels with accessible validation text.

output_examples.input: A custom menu component that opens on click and contains several actions.
output_examples.output: The response explains required keyboard behavior, focus movement, accessible names, and ARIA roles only where native elements are insufficient.

output_examples.input: A page layout with skipped heading levels and unclear landmarks.
output_examples.output: The audit suggests a logical heading order, landmark improvements, and clearer navigation structure for screen reader users.

best_practices: Prefer native HTML controls before adding ARIA roles or custom interaction models.
Test important flows with keyboard-only navigation and at least one screen reader.
Verify contrast for text, controls, focus indicators, disabled states, and error states.
anti_patterns: Do not use clickable div elements when a button or link is the correct control.
Do not hide focus indicators or depend only on pointer interactions.
Do not add ARIA attributes without matching behavior and accessible names.

faq.question: Does this skill run automated accessibility tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation and review guidance that can complement automated tests.

faq.question: Can it help with WCAG requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It prompts checks for common WCAG concerns like contrast, semantics, keyboard access, and focus visibility.

faq.question: Does it support React projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is designed for React components in TSX and JSX files.

faq.question: Can it review forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on labels, input relationships, validation messages, and completion by keyboard users.

faq.question: Can it replace screen reader testing?
faq.answer: No. Manual testing remains necessary for important flows and assistive technology behavior.

faq.question: Why is the audit warning about a file path?
faq.answer: The skill references a file outside its own directory, so the author should inline that guidance or package it safely.
